Subject: Intro + proposed demo-credit and prospect protection framework

Hi Elena / Rajiv —

Great speaking with you yesterday. As promised, putting our proposed framework in writing so we have a clear starting point for commercial and ops to review. High level asks from AcmeCloud were: 1) predictable demo credits for qualifying prospects, 2) short-term prospect lock (proof-of-intro) to avoid conflict with other partners, and 3) clear clawback rules for no-shows / disqualified leads.

Proposed (initial, flexible):
- Demo credits: up to 10 free hosted demo sessions per quarter credited to AcmeCloud (applies to prospects introduced via partner lead registration).
- Prospect lock (proof-of-intro): 30 days from registration to qualify for credit; if customer signs within 30 days, credit applies to the first bill.
- Commission: Standard referral % (to be confirmed by revenue ops) once paid usage exceeds trial thresholds.
- Clawback: Credit reclaimed if prospect fails to engage after 90 days or is identified as duplicate with earlier partner.

I've attached a light MOU/draft that captures the above and a simple demo-credit matrix so legal and partner ops can iterate. Camila/Marissa/Ben — can you review and flag any operational risks?

Next actions:
1) Camila: propose onboarding steps and registration flow (we need minimal friction but clear evidence for proof-of-intro).
2) Marissa/Ben: confirm commission band and how demo credits map to deal credit accounting.
3) Elena/Rajiv: confirm that 30-day lock is acceptable and whether Acme needs a longer exclusivity window for named targets.

Thanks — looking forward to a quick loop.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Head of Partner GTM
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Acme_Redwood_MOU-draft.pdf (stub), demo-credit-matrix.xlsx (stub)

Jordan — thanks for the clear note. 30 days for proof-of-intro is reasonable for most inbound names, but for named-top-account targets we typically request 60 days to avoid mid-cycle conflicts with other vendors. A few clarifications:

- Demo credits: are these per-account or per-contact? We book demos against accounts; would prefer account-level credits.
- Qualification: what are the exact criteria for a prospect to be 'introduced' (e.g., first-touch email thread + HubSpot lead created)?
- Tracking: can we get a weekly feed or HubSpot sync so we can reconcile registrations quickly?

We can accept a 30-day default if AcmeCloud can request 60-day named-account protection on a case-by-case basis (we'll put a list of up to 5 named accounts per quarter).

I'll loop in our partnerships legal if we move toward an MOU, but the draft looks like a good start.

–Elena
Partnerships Lead, AcmeCloud

Thanks Jordan — quick operational notes from partner ops:

1) Registration evidence: we prefer a lightweight form + HubSpot lead creation. Proof-of-intro should include the first email thread or a HubSpot lead id created by the partner (time-stamped).
2) Account-level credits: fine — we'll map credits to the top-level account ID in our billing system. That avoids contact churn.
3) Named-account protection: we can support a 60-day exception for up to 5 named accounts per quarter, but those must be pre-registered in a shared Drive sheet and approved by Redwood partner ops (Camila).
4) Clawback rules: propose 75% reclamation for duplicate detection within 90 days, 100% if partner materially misrepresents the lead (legal to define).

I've updated the MOU draft (attached) to reflect account-level credits, a named-account exception process, and an operational checklist for onboarding demo users. Also included a simple webhook spec so Acme can push registrations to our partner intake endpoint — that will allow near real-time reconciliation.

Attaching: Acme_Redwood_MOU-draft.pdf (updated), demo-credit-matrix.xlsx

Camila
